exercise.name: Dumbbell Lying on Floor Rear Delt Raise

reference.title: Dumbbell Lying on Floor Rear Delt Raise
reference.listing: Page not read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the dumbbells lift, breathe in as they lower to the floor.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, 1 s hold, about 1.5 s down

prescription.load: Light dumbbells; the range is short but the arms are long levers
prescription.progression: Longer holds at the top, then heavier dumbbells

cues.text: Lie face down on the mat, forehead just off the floor. Arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height, dumbbells resting on the floor, palms down.
Breathe out and lift both dumbbells off the floor by squeezing the shoulder blades together; arms stay long.
Hold a moment with the arms a few inches off the floor; the chest stays down.
Breathe in and lower slowly until the dumbbells touch the floor.
Touch lightly, keep tension, and repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the chest and arching the back
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest and the hips on the floor; only the arms rise.

mistakes.mistake: Shrugging the shoulders to the ears
mistakes.fix: Draw the shoulder blades back and down.

mistakes.mistake: Bending the elbows to lift higher
mistakes.fix: Keep the arms long; the range is short.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping the dumbbells to the floor

kinematics.norm: Arms lift a few inches above the floor at about 90 degrees of abduction; prone horizontal abduction at 100 degrees gave high posterior deltoid EMG (Reinold 2007)
Arms out to the sides at shoulder height, palms down (clinical opinion); a thumbs-up grip raised posterior shoulder activity (Schoenfeld 2013)
Chest and hips stay on the floor (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #13810, Dumbbell Lying on Floor Rear Delt Raise, video (movement reference only; page not read)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Keep the neck long; rest the forehead on a folded towel if needed.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: bend the elbows to 90 degrees (shorter lever).
Neck discomfort: rest the forehead on a towel.

muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Prime mover: lifts the arm back from the floor (horizontal abduction); about 87% MVIC in prone horizontal abduction (Reinold 2007).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Prime mover: lifts the arm back from the floor (horizontal abduction); about 87% MVIC in prone horizontal abduction (Reinold 2007).
